objective: Show the evidence class of every scenario in the read-only dashboard, sourced from the generated readiness report, so a scripted fixture run cannot be read as a released capability, and report a missing or stale report as an explicit unavailable state rather than a blank panel.
decision_supported: Can a person looking at the dashboard tell which evidence axis a run actually reaches and whether it is release eligible, without reading the generated JSON by hand?
acceptance: The dashboard shows, per scenario, the evidence class and the four axis flags, sourced from the committed report rather than re-derived in the browser.
Every confirmed run is visibly labelled SCRIPTED_FIXTURE with release_eligible: false when that is its class, and a run whose class is NOT_EXECUTED or BLOCKED says so and shows no success styling.
The success styling is decided by the server (renders_as_success) and read by the page, so a template cannot invent its own rule about whether a fixture looks green.
A missing or stale readiness report is a visible unavailable state carrying the reason, not a blank panel, and the page says the class is unknown rather than absent.
A report whose evidence_classes is missing an axis is unavailable rather than treated as false, because false is a claim and a missing key is not readable.
The page is still read-only: no control, no mutation endpoint, and the existing read-only contract test keeps passing unchanged.
The evidence-class rendering is tested at the JSON and script level, so a change that maps scripted_fixture onto success styling fails a test rather than shipping.
The readiness report itself is unchanged: make readiness-report-check passes and the report is not regenerated by this change.
evidence: pytest output for tests/unit/test_dashboard_backend.py: 56 passed, of which 11 are the new evidence-class tests.
The endpoint payload showing every committed scenario at SCRIPTED_FIXTURE, release_eligible false, renders_as_success false, software and scripted_fixture reached, gazebo and physical not reached.
The unavailable payload from a directory with no report: available false, scenarios empty, summary null, and a message that says the class is unknown rather than absent.
The missing-axis payload: available false with a reason naming the axis, so a partial report cannot be read as false.
make readiness-report-check output: PASS, 5 scenario rows match the report this checkout generates, unchanged.
make docs PASS, ruff check and ruff format --check clean.
A full make test comparison against the unmodified main baseline showing the same pre-existing environment-blocked failures and no new ones.
stop_conditions: The work would require a new field in the readiness report; that report is generated by tools/scripts/readiness_report.py and changing its shape is its own issue under the evaluation owner.
The work would require a write endpoint or a control; the dashboard is read-only by contract and this issue adds no mutation.
A write outside allowed_paths is required, especially to the generated report or to the generator.
Showing the class would require re-deriving it from run fixtures rather than reading the generated report, which would give the UI a second source of truth.
data_classification: Repository-local HTML, JavaScript, Python and a committed generated JSON report. The page is read-only, serves no credential and copies no evidence path.
model_policy: Deterministic Python and static front-end assets; no model inference and no network access added by this change beyond the existing local backend fetch.
risks_and_fallbacks: A table of classes could be read as a progress bar. The page states the axes weakest-first, prints `release_eligible: false` on every non-released row, and shows the four axes as reached or absent rather than as a score.

The unavailable state could be mistaken for an empty report. It is its own panel with a message that says the class is unknown and a reason, and the metric row and scenario table are hidden while it is shown.

The page depends on the generated report's shape. That dependency is explicit: an unknown status, a missing axis or a non-boolean release_eligible is unavailable rather than a guess, so a report change surfaces as a visible state instead of a silently wrong colour.
Rollback is a revert of this commit: remove the panel and the endpoint. The dashboard returns to its current tables, no other view consumes the class data, and the report is untouched either way.
